significance.justification: Verified true, the claim would establish that a teacher using a "conditional steering vector" can transmit through "semantically-unrelated data" a student trait that remains dormant normally and activates under a trigger "without the trigger ever appearing in the training data"; this is a form-(iii) binary gating relation between trigger context and trait strength, supported by a form-(ii) causal steering mechanism. It establishes both a consequential phenomenon and an internal account, constraining expectations for clean-versus-triggered behavior and the decision to treat trigger-token scanning as sufficient; this matters in light of Cloud et al.'s subliminal trait transmission and Hubinger et al.'s Sleeper Agents, where conditional policies are a concrete deployment concern. A verified-false result would still be informative by ruling out trigger-absent conditional transmission within the asserted same-base-model setting, separating subliminal transfer of global traits from installation of dormant policies; true and false therefore name distinct states of the world. Topic substitution check: merely restating "extend subliminal learning" would not support this score—the absent-trigger conditional dependence and inherited gating mechanism are the claim-specific reasons it sits above the topic median.

reach.justification: The named handles are an intervention—the "conditional steering direction"—a measurable diagnostic, "trigger-selectivity (triggered/untriggered strength ratio)," and the design constraint that audits examine "training provenance and dynamics rather than data contents alone." The steering intervention and provenance constraint are ex ante because they can affect model construction or screening before deployment, whereas trigger-selectivity is principally a post-hoc diagnostic; the claim does not hand defenders a concrete detector guaranteed to find an unknown trigger. After per-model re-extraction, the conclusion predicts qualitative gated activation and failure of content-based trigger scanning, but it does not predict a universal direction or numerical attack-success rate; its stated limitations narrow scope to largely same-base-model settings, while downstream uptake includes fine-tuning-data auditors and model shippers. Topic substitution check: the general importance of subliminal learning would not earn this reach score; the transferable absent-trigger threat model, audit constraint, and ex-ante conditional-steering handle do.
